note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as published by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Every guide below is written in our own words from those descriptions and from general GTA knowledge. GTA VI launched on 19 November 2026, the day this guide was written, so any step that depends on a location, a menu name or a count the community has not yet confirmed in-game is flagged inside the guide as unverified — treat those lines as a best lead, not a promise, and check the in-game pause menu before committing hours to them.

roadmap.title: Story, part one — learn Leonida
roadmap.summary: Play Chapters 1 and 2 in order, meet the strangers, and keep a manual save before every mission that smells like a choice. Nothing here needs grinding; just finish the story beats and the early stranger introductions.

roadmap.title: Story, part two — to the finale
roadmap.summary: Clear Chapters 3 and 4, the heists and the final mission, and finish every stranger strand. This is where most story trophies land, including the two golds' setup work.

roadmap.title: Open world — activities and collectibles
roadmap.summary: With the map fully open and fast travel unlocked, work through the activities (races, fishing, arcade, meditation, hunting), the card sets, the WAiNK spots and the exploration trophies.

roadmap.title: The counted grinds and the money
roadmap.summary: The long numbers: 250 stunts, 50 challenges, 100 vehicles, bank vaults, armored trucks, gang operations, and the two money trophies. Do these after the story, when you own the full weapon set and know the roads.

roadmap.title: 100% completion and the platinum
roadmap.summary: Sweep the in-game 100% checklist — it is the only thing standing between you and the two golds — then watch the platinum pop with the last trophy you earn.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: There is no separate task for the platinum: it unlocks by itself the moment the other 54 trophies are all yours, so the whole of this guide is the guide for it. The honest shape of the run is about 60 to 100 hours — the story is the short part, and the cleanup is where the hours go. Work the five roadmap stages in order (story first, strangers and activities next, the counted grinds after that, 100% completion last) and use the checklist on this page to see what is left at a glance, ticking trophies off as you earn them so the final push is never a mystery. If you are short on time, leave the long grinds — 250 stunts, 50 challenges, the Shooting Range golds — until after the finale, when you own the full weapon set and know the map well enough to farm efficiently. The last trophy you earn will almost certainly be A Long Road, the 100% completion gold; when it pops, the platinum follows within seconds.
steps: Clear every story trophy in roadmap stages 1 and 2 by playing the chapters in order
Finish all eight stranger strands and their final missions in stage 2
Work through the activities, collectibles and exploration trophies in stage 3
Grind the counted trophies — stunts, races, challenges, Shooting Range golds — in stage 4
Open Stats and check the in-game 100% tracker before the final push
Earn the last remaining trophy; the platinum pops with it
tips: Read the Missables tab before you start the story — five trophies need a manual save at the right moment
Do the counted grinds after the story, when you own the full weapon set and know the map
Keep one rotating manual save slot all the way through, separate from autosaves
pitfalls: Chasing the platinum before finishing the story wastes hours — most grinds are faster with late-game gear
A single missed choice trophy can force a second playthrough, so save before any mission that offers a choice

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is an early story mission — the fishing trip that introduces the fishing activity — and this trophy pops when you finish it, with no extra requirement beyond completing the mission itself. You cannot miss it by playing badly: story missions in GTA can be retried from the pause menu, so even a failed attempt just sends you back to the start of the mission. Expect a short drive to a pier or a boat, a scripted fishing sequence that teaches you the cast-and-reel controls, and a drive back; the mission also unlocks fishing as a free-roam activity, which matters later for Baited My Tackle, the trophy for beating Cal in a fishing challenge. Play it when it appears in Chapter 1 and move on — there is nothing to prepare, no gear to buy first, and no choice to get wrong.
steps: Play through Chapter 1 until the Gone Fishing mission marker appears
Drive to the marker and start the mission
Follow the on-screen fishing prompts — cast, wait for the bite, reel steadily
Finish the mission's closing drive and let the trophy pop
tips: The fishing controls you learn here are the same ones the later fishing challenge uses, so pay attention to the reel timing
If you fail the mission, retry it from the pause menu — the trophy only needs one completion
pitfalls: None — this is an unmissable story trophy, but it only counts when the mission fully completes, not on a checkpoint

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.time: A few hours of story play
trophies.guide: Paradise Lost is the reward for finishing Chapter 1, the opening act of the story — Lucia and Jason's setup in Leonida, the first heists and the first strangers. There is nothing to do for it beyond playing the chapter's missions in order until the chapter-end cutscene rolls; every mission in the chapter counts toward it, and the trophy pops at the chapter card, not during a mission. Chapters in GTA VI are long — expect several hours of missions, drives and cutscenes — and the game will tell you when a chapter turns over. If you are chasing the platinum efficiently, do not detour into side activities during Chapter 1: the map, the stranger strands and most activities open up properly afterwards, and the early game is better spent learning the driving and combat than grinding. Just follow the mission markers and the trophy takes care of itself.
steps: Start a new game and follow the Chapter 1 mission markers in order
Complete each mission — retry any failed mission from the pause menu
Watch for the chapter-end sequence after the last Chapter 1 mission
The trophy pops at the chapter card
tips: Save the side activities for after Chapter 1, when more of the map and its systems are open
Keep a manual save at the start of each play session in case a mission bugs out
pitfalls: Skipping cutscenes cannot skip the trophy, but quitting mid-mission before a checkpoint can cost you the mission's progress

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: This is the Chapter 2 completion trophy, and like Paradise Lost it asks nothing more than finishing the chapter's missions in order. Chapter 2 is where the story widens: more of Leonida opens up, the stranger strands start appearing in earnest, and the first real heist planning begins, so expect a longer stretch of missions than Chapter 1, with more driving between Vice City and the surrounding counties. The trophy pops at the chapter-end card. One practical note for the road ahead: by the end of Chapter 2 you will have met several of the strangers whose final missions carry trophies of their own (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), so take the introductions when they appear rather than leaving every stranger for the post-game — their strands are long, and starting them early spreads the work out. Otherwise, just play the story and let the trophy arrive on its own.
steps: Continue from Chapter 1 into Chapter 2 and follow the mission markers
Complete each Chapter 2 mission in order, retrying failures from the pause menu
Take stranger introductions as they appear — their strands are long
Finish the last Chapter 2 mission and the trophy pops at the chapter card
tips: Start stranger strands early; their final missions are trophies and the strands take hours
Explore the newly opened map between missions — the Goodtime State exploration trophy rewards it later
pitfalls: Leaving every stranger introduction until after the story compresses hours of strand missions into the endgame

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Vice City, Baby! marks the end of Chapter 3, the point where the story is fully in Vice City proper and the stakes — and the mission difficulty — step up. The missions here lean harder on driving chases, shootouts and multi-stage heist setups, so by now you should be comfortable with Combat Focus, cover and the weapon wheel; if a mission keeps failing, drop the difficulty in the pause menu rather than burning an evening on one shootout, since the trophy only needs the chapter finished, not finished stylishly. The trophy pops at the chapter-end card after the last Chapter 3 mission. This is also a good moment to check your stranger strands: several of them gate their later missions behind story progress, so if a stranger has gone quiet, pushing the story forward is usually what wakes them up again.
steps: Play the Chapter 3 missions in order from the end of Chapter 2
Use cover and Combat Focus in the heavier shootouts; lower the difficulty if a mission stalls you
Check in with strangers between missions — story progress unlocks their next steps
Finish the last Chapter 3 mission; the trophy pops at the chapter card
tips: Stock up on ammo and armour before the chapter's bigger set-pieces — the general stores sell both
If a stranger strand stalls, advance the story; most strands gate on chapter progress
pitfalls: Grinding side content mid-chapter can leave you under-levelled for the chapter's harder missions — the story gives you the gear as you go

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Top Of The World, Ma is the Chapter 4 completion trophy — the last chapter before the finale — and it lands the same way as the other chapter trophies: finish the chapter's missions in order and the trophy pops at the chapter card. Chapter 4 is the endgame of the story, so expect the longest and hardest missions in the game here, including the big heist setups that the earlier chapters were building toward; the Cartel Heist and VCIA Takedown missions both sit in this stretch of the game, and each carries its own trophy too. Before you start the chapter, spend a few minutes preparing: buy full armour and ammo, keep a fast car and a bike in your garage, and make a manual save — not because the chapter can be missed, but because the finale that follows it is where the missable choice trophies live, and you want a clean save to fall back on. Once Chapter 4 is done, only the final mission stands between you and the story's end.
steps: Prepare before starting: full armour, ammo, a fast car and a bike garaged
Make a manual save — the finale after this chapter holds the choice trophies
Play the Chapter 4 missions in order, including the heist setups
Finish the last Chapter 4 mission; the trophy pops at the chapter card
tips: The Cartel Heist and VCIA Takedown missions in this chapter each have their own trophy — play them when they appear
A manual save before the chapter is cheap insurance for the finale's choices
pitfalls: Rushing into the finale without a manual save leaves you no way back if a choice trophy goes the wrong way

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: This gold is the story's finish line: complete the final mission and it pops. The final mission is long and multi-stage — expect driving, a big shootout and a closing sequence with both protagonists — so set aside an uninterrupted hour, stock up on armour and ammo first, and do not start it at 1 a.m. The one thing that matters more than the mission itself is what happens around it: the finale is where the game's big choices live, and at least two trophies in this list (Actions Speak Louder and Bad Luck, I Guess) read like they hinge on choices made here, so make a manual save before you start the final mission and keep it until both of those trophies are confirmed in your list. If a choice trophy does not pop, reload that save and take the other path rather than replaying the whole game. The trophy itself is unmissable — the final mission can always be retried — but the choices around it are the one place in the game where a wrong turn costs real time.
steps: Finish Chapter 4, then make a manual save before starting the final mission
Stock armour, ammo and a fast getaway vehicle
Play the final mission through all of its stages — retry from checkpoints if you fail
Let the credits roll; the gold pops when the mission completes
tips: Save before the finale and keep that save until the choice trophies are confirmed
If a choice trophy does not pop, reload the pre-finale save and take the other path
pitfalls: Starting the finale without a manual save is the single most expensive mistake in the whole platinum run
The final mission is long — do not start it without time to finish it in one sitting

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is an early story mission, and Trust pops when you finish it. It is listed here as possibly missable — not because the mission itself can be failed permanently (story missions can always be retried), but because its name and placement suggest a timed or partner-dependent setup: a morning run with your partner that may only be offered in a narrow story window, and the community has not yet confirmed whether it can be replayed after the story moves on. The safe play costs you nothing: when the Breakfast Run marker appears in Chapter 1 or 2, play it immediately instead of wandering off to side content, and make a manual save just before you start it. If the mission does turn out to be replayable later, you have lost nothing but a save slot; if it is a one-time window, you have saved yourself a second playthrough. Unverified at the time of writing — the game launched the day this guide was built — so treat the warning as cheap insurance rather than a confirmed fact.
steps: Watch for the Breakfast Run marker in the early chapters and make a manual save first
Play the mission as soon as it appears — do not leave it for later
Complete the mission's drive and objectives; retry from the pause menu if you fail
The trophy pops when the mission completes
tips: Play story missions the moment they appear if their names suggest a one-time window
A manual save before any partner mission is free insurance
pitfalls: Possibly missable (unverified): leaving this mission unplayed while the story advances may close its window

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is one of the story's big set-piece heists, and Break the Bank pops when you complete it. Heists in GTA VI run in phases — planning and setup missions first, then the heist itself — so if the trophy has not popped after a setup mission, that is normal: the setups are separate missions, and only the finale counts. Come prepared with full armour, a good rifle and a fast getaway car, and expect a multi-stage job with a stealth or loud approach, a vault or stash grab, and a chase out. The heist is unmissable — it is a story mission, so it can be retried — but the setups are worth doing carefully, because the heist's payout feeds the money trophies later (Dime on the Dollar wants $250,000 laundered, and Treat Yo Self wants $100,000 spent). Play the setups when they appear in Chapter 4, then run the heist itself and collect the trophy at the end.
steps: Play the Cartel Heist setup missions when they appear in Chapter 4
Stock armour, a rifle and a fast getaway car before the finale
Run the heist: get in, grab the take, and survive the escape
The trophy pops when the heist mission completes
tips: The heist payout feeds the money trophies — bank the take rather than spending it all at once
Setup missions are separate from the finale; only the finale pops the trophy
pitfalls: Starting the heist finale under-geared turns a scripted escape into a repeated failure — prepare first

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Family Matters pops when you finish Child's Play, a story mission whose name points at a family thread in Lucia or Jason's life. Like every story-mission trophy it is unmissable: follow the story markers until the mission unlocks, play it through, and retry from the pause menu if any section beats you. Family missions in GTA have a habit of ending in a firefight, so stock armour before you start and keep a sturdy car nearby for the exit — the mission is short, but the last stretch can get loud. Beyond that, there is nothing to prepare and no choice to get wrong; the trophy is a pure progress marker on the way through the chapters, and it pops at the mission-complete screen.
steps: Play the story until the Child's Play marker appears
Stock armour and keep a sturdy car nearby
Follow the mission objectives to the end
Retry from the pause menu if a section fails
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen
tips: Family missions tend to end in a firefight — armour first, questions later
Play it when it appears; there is no reason to delay a story mission
pitfalls: None — the mission is unmissable and retriable, so the only cost of failure is a minute of your time

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: DWNFALL is the trophy for completing Headliners, a story mission whose name points at a show-business thread — a venue, a crowd, a headline act. Expect a set-piece that mixes on-foot sections with a driving escape: follow the objective prompts as they appear rather than fighting the crowd, keep a vehicle in mind for the exit leg, and do not get boxed in when the scene turns chaotic. It is unmissable like every story mission — retry from the pause menu if you fail — and it pops at the mission-complete screen. Headliners sits in the middle stretch of the story, so by the time it appears you should be comfortable with the driving and the shooting; if the escape leg keeps failing, switch to a faster car and take the highways instead of the side streets.
steps: Play the story until the Headliners marker appears
Follow the set-piece prompts as they appear on screen
Keep a fast vehicle ready for the escape leg
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the complete screen
tips: In crowd set-pieces, follow the objective marker rather than fighting the crowd
A fast car on the highway beats a quick car through side streets on the escape leg
pitfalls: Getting boxed in by a crowd during the set-piece — keep moving toward the objective marker, not through the densest crowd

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Hi-Jacked pops when you complete the VCIA Takedown at Vice City International Airport. Airport missions mean runways, hangars and a getaway: keep a fast vehicle ready for the escape leg and expect a wanted level on the way out — break line of sight, leave the search area, and do not stop to fight the airport police once you are clear of the objective. While you are there, learn the runway layout: the airport is also home to Catch Me If You Can, the trophy for making an unscheduled departure in a stolen plane, so any plane parking spot you note during this mission is one you can come back for later. The mission itself is unmissable and retriable, and the trophy pops when it completes.
steps: Play the story until the VCIA Takedown marker appears
Keep a fast vehicle ready for the escape
Complete the takedown objectives inside the airport
Break line of sight and leave the search area on the escape
The trophy pops when the mission completes
tips: Note where planes park — you will want one later for Catch Me If You Can
Expect a wanted level on the escape; hide in a parking garage or alley until it clears
pitfalls: Stopping to fight airport police during the escape — the wanted level only clears once you leave the search area

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Snow Storm is the trophy for Operation Savage Glory, a military-flavoured story mission — the name alone promises a heavy combat sequence. Stock armour, a good rifle and plenty of ammo before you start, fight from cover, and lean on Combat Focus in the big firefights; the same skill comes back as its own trophy (Gunslinger, five enemies in one Combat Focus), so this mission is good practice. Expect waves rather than a single push: clear each wave from cover before advancing, and do not sprint into open ground between waves. If the same section keeps beating you, drop the difficulty in the pause menu for that mission — the trophy does not care what difficulty you played on. It is unmissable, retriable, and pops at the mission-complete screen.
steps: Play the story until Operation Savage Glory unlocks
Buy armour, rifle ammo and snacks first
Clear each enemy wave from cover before advancing
Use Combat Focus in the big firefights
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen
tips: A scoped rifle helps in the open sections; a shotgun helps in the close ones — carry both if you can
Combat Focus practice here pays off for the Gunslinger trophy
pitfalls: Advancing into open ground between waves — clear the wave first, then move
Starting a heavy combat mission without armour or rifle ammo

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: A Long Road is the gold for attaining 100% completion, and for most players it will be the last trophy before the platinum. The in-game Stats screen shows the 100% checklist — story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the counted grinds — and it is the only authority on what counts: the exact 100% requirements were not fully confirmed by the community at launch, so treat the in-game tracker as the source of truth, not any checklist on the internet. Work through this guide's roadmap stage by stage and check the tracker after each stage so you know which category is holding you back. When the tracker hits 100%, this trophy pops, and the platinum usually follows within seconds. The one thing that can strand this trophy is a missed choice trophy among the five flagged as possibly missable — if one of those is gone, 100% may be unreachable without a second playthrough, which is why the manual saves matter.
steps: Open Stats to see the 100% checklist and what it counts
Finish the story, the stranger strands, the activities and the collectibles
Clear the counted grinds — stunts, races, challenges
Re-check the tracker after each category; it names what is left
The trophy pops when the tracker hits 100%
tips: The tracker is the authority: if a category reads short, that category is your next job
Do the grinds last — story and side content fill most of the tracker on their own
pitfalls: Trusting an online 100% checklist over the in-game tracker — the tracker is what the game counts
Leaving a possibly-missable trophy behind: the five flagged trophies can block 100% if they are gone

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Cunning Stunts is the silver for completing 250 stunts — stunt jumps, near-misses, airtime and similar driving feats, all tracked across the whole game. This is a pure grind and it belongs after the story, when you know the map and own a fast bike and a fast car. The fastest farm is the highway: a fast car weaving past traffic without touching it chains near-misses far quicker than hunting individual stunt jumps, and a highway run also racks up airtime on the crests. Use the stunt-jump ramps marked around Leonida to break up the highway runs — each jump counts once per ramp, so rotate between ramps rather than repeating one. Your count is on the Stats screen: check it before you start grinding so you know how far the story already took you, and check it again every half hour so the number keeps moving.
steps: Check your stunt count in Stats before you start
Take a fast bike to the marked stunt-jump ramps and rotate between them
Chain near-misses and airtime on busy highways in a fast car
Repeat until the count hits 250 — it stacks across all play
tips: Near-misses on a busy highway are the fastest farm: speed past traffic without touching it
Check the Stats count every half hour so you can see the grind working
pitfalls: Crashing ends a near-miss chain — brake early and pick gaps in traffic instead of threading them at full speed
Repeating one stunt jump: it counts once per ramp, so rotate

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Master of None asks you to try each type of activity once — fishing, the Shooting Range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting, racing and the stranger activities. You do not need to be good at any of them: one attempt each counts, and a last-place finish still counts as a try. Work through the activity icons on the map and tick each off as you go; most unlock early in the story, so this is a trophy to pick up during the story rather than a grind for later. The exact list of activity types was not fully confirmed at launch, so use the in-game activity list as the authority: if a type shows as untried there, that is your next stop, and if the trophy has not popped after you have tried everything on the map, the missing type is probably a stranger activity you have not met yet.
steps: Open the map and note every activity icon
Try one of each: fish, shoot, race, bowl, meditate, hunt
Arcade games and drone races count too
The trophy pops on the last new activity type
tips: Do this during the story — most activities unlock early and the attempts are quick
One attempt is enough; do not grind any activity for this trophy
pitfalls: Assuming the list is fixed: check the in-game activity menu, since the exact set was unconfirmed at launch
Grinding an activity for score when one attempt is all this trophy needs

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shootist is the silver for earning a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, per the official list's progress target — and it is the hardest skill trophy in the game. Each challenge scores accuracy, time and headshots, so expect to replay the hard ones several times; your best medal is kept, so every attempt is progress and a silver today is a gold tomorrow once you learn the target order. Use the recommended weapon for each challenge, shoot from a stable position where the rules allow it, and start with the challenges you are closest to gold on — quick wins build the habit and the confidence. Save the hardest weapon types for last, when your aim is warm, and do the whole thing after the story, when you own the full weapon set and have ammo to burn. Headshots score far more than body shots, so slow down and aim for the head on precision challenges; on timed ones, learn the target order with a slow run first, then race it.
steps: Visit a Shooting Range and try each of the 42 challenges
Match the recommended weapon to each challenge
Replay for gold — your best medal is kept
Work easiest-first and save the hardest weapon types for last
The trophy pops at 42 gold medals
tips: Headshots score far more than body shots — slow down and aim for the head on precision challenges
If a challenge has a time bonus, learn the target order first with a slow run, then race it
pitfalls: Burning all your ammo on one challenge: switch challenges when you stall and come back fresh
Rushing timed challenges before learning the target order
sources: PSNProfiles — progress target: 42 Shooting Range challenges

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun wants a win in a Top Fun Drone Race at every location. Drone races are time trials through rings: learn each track with a slow practice run first, then race it cleanly. Cut corners only where the rings allow it and keep the drone low and steady through the gates — altitude changes cost more time than they save, and a missed ring costs more than a slow line. Every location needs a win, not just a finish, so a second-place run at a location does not count and you will need to go back for it. The locations are spread across Leonida, so pair each race with nearby exploration for The Goodtime State and the WAiNK locations — one road trip can feed three trophies at once.
steps: Find each Top Fun Drone Race location on the map
Practice the track once before racing it
Race cleanly through every ring — a win is required
Win at every location; a finish is not enough
tips: A slow practice run that learns the ring order beats three fast runs that miss a gate
Keep the drone low and steady; climbing and diving wastes seconds on every ring
pitfalls: Missing a ring: most races fail on one missed gate, not on raw speed
Treating a finish as a win — every location needs first place

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Earn Cash, Not Kudos wants 20 different race wins. Races count per distinct event, so winning the same race twice does not help — you need 20 different ones across street races, off-road and whatever else the map offers. Race during the story when events appear and mop up the rest after; a fast tuned car and clean racing lines matter more than aggression, and ramming rivals usually costs you more time than it costs them. Check the race list in the game to see which events you have already won, and prioritise the ones you have not tried yet — a fresh event is always worth more than a repeat. If a race keeps beating you, change the car: a tuned car with good grip beats a faster car that slides off every corner, and the right car for a dirt track is rarely the right car for a street circuit.
steps: Enter races from map markers and contacts
Win 20 different events — repeats do not count
Use a fast tuned car and clean racing lines
Check the race list to see which events are still unwon
tips: Learn each track with one slow lap before racing it for the win
A tuned car with good grip beats a faster car that slides off every corner
pitfalls: Re-winning a race you already won: it feels like progress and counts for nothing
Ramming rivals instead of racing clean — it costs you more time than it costs them

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Baited My Tackle is the trophy for beating Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are head-to-head: catch the target fish faster, or more of them, than Cal. Use the best rod and bait you have, watch the line tension, and reel steadily — snapping the line wastes the most time, and a snapped line during a challenge is usually the difference between winning and losing. Cal is a named rival, so the challenge unlocks through the fishing thread; keep fishing until it appears, and fish in the spots the thread points you to rather than at random. If you lose, you can retry the challenge — the trophy is about the win, not the first attempt — so treat the first try as a scouting run and go back with better gear if you need to.
steps: Fish until the challenge against Cal appears
Use your best rod and bait
Reel steadily — do not snap the line
Out-fish Cal to win the challenge
tips: Buy the best rod and bait you can afford before the challenge — gear is the biggest edge
Watch the tension meter, not the fish: steady reeling with pauses beats frantic reeling
pitfalls: Snapping the line by reeling through a strong run — ease off when the fish fights
Fishing at random spots instead of the ones the thread points to

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Stick Fiddler pops when you complete an arcade game. Find an arcade machine — in bars, arcades and some businesses around Vice City — and play one game through to its end. Any game counts; pick the shortest one you find. No score target is needed, just a completed run, so do not chase a high score when a quick finish is all the trophy asks for. If the first machine's game is long or hard, walk away and try another machine — the trophy counts any completed game on any machine, and the shortest game in the building is the right one for this trophy. It is a five-minute trophy once you find a machine, so grab it during the story whenever you pass an arcade.
steps: Find an arcade machine in Vice City
Start any arcade game — pick the shortest one
Play it through to completion
The trophy pops when the game ends
tips: Bars and arcades are the densest places to find machines
A short game beats a high score: finish, do not chase points
pitfalls: Quitting a game early — only a completed run counts
Chasing a high score when a quick finish is all the trophy asks

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Road to Rehabilitation is the trophy for completing the final mission for Andy, one of the stranger characters. Stranger strands unlock from question-mark markers around Leonida; play Andy's missions in order until the strand ends. Stranger missions stay available after the story, so this can be done during cleanup — but do not leave all eight strands to the very end, or the cleanup stage becomes a long slog of back-to-back stranger missions. Andy's strand is one of the five named stranger trophies, and all five count toward the eight strands the Strangers & Freaks silver needs, so finishing Andy is progress on two trophies at once. Start a few strands during the story to spread the work out, and finish each one completely before starting the next — half-finished strands are easy to forget.
steps: Find Andy's question-mark marker on the map
Play Andy's missions in order
Finish the strand's final mission
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen
tips: Stranger strands stay open after the story — do two or three during the story to spread the work
Each named stranger strand counts toward the 8-strand silver
pitfalls: Leaving every stranger strand for post-story cleanup — spread them across the playthrough
Starting strands and never finishing them: only completed strands count

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: This Was No Boat Accident is the trophy for completing the final mission for Kenton, another stranger — and the name is a nod to a famous shark film, which tells you what to expect: water and boats. Find Kenton's marker, play his missions in order, finish the last one. Expect boat sections and a chase on the water, so learn the boat controls early — water chases punish drivers who only know cars, and a boat handles nothing like a car in a turn. Like the other stranger strands it stays available after the story, and it counts toward the eight strands the silver needs, so it is progress on two trophies at once.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: The Lone Rider is the trophy for completing the final mission for Billy, a stranger, and the name points at bikes. Find Billy's marker, play the strand through, finish the last mission. Keep a good motorcycle handy for his missions — and remember that bikes are also the best vehicles for stunt jumps, so Billy's strand pairs well with the 250-stunt grind: ride to his missions on a bike and you will be earning stunts on the way. Bikes are fragile in shootouts, though, so park the bike and fight on foot when the shooting starts rather than getting shot off it. The strand stays available after the story and counts toward the eight strands the silver needs.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers & Freaks is the silver for completing 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida. There are more than eight strangers, so you can pick the easiest eight — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone all have their own trophies, and three more strands complete the set. Explore for question-mark markers, especially outside Vice City, and finish strands one at a time rather than starting all of them at once: half-finished strands are easy to forget, and the trophy only counts completed ones. The strands stay open after the story, so this is a stage-3 cleanup trophy, but starting a few during the story keeps the cleanup short — and the rural markers are the ones players miss, so drive the back roads, not just the highways, when you are hunting for them.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Supply & Demand is the trophy for completing the final mission for Randy, a stranger whose thread ties to the supply-and-demand economy. Expect delivery and deal missions — driving goods from one place to another under pressure, sometimes with rivals or police in pursuit — so a fast, sturdy car matters more here than firepower. On delivery legs, the shortest route is not always the fastest: highways beat shortcuts through traffic, and a route you have driven before is worth more than a shortcut you have not. Find Randy's marker, play his missions in order, finish the last one. The strand stays open after the story and counts toward the eight strands the silver needs.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Spin On This! is the trophy for completing the final mission for Tyrone, a stranger — and his name is a DJ nod, so expect music-venue missions around Vice City nightlife: clubs, crowds and late-night driving. Night missions can make it harder to spot objectives, so follow the marker rather than the scenery, and in nightclub sections walk rather than sprinting, or you will shove the wrong person into a fight. Find Tyrone's marker, play his missions in order, finish the last one. The strand stays open after the story and counts toward the eight strands the silver needs.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Positive Mental Attitude wants you to meditate at every spot across Leonida. Meditation spots are scenic viewpoints — beaches, hilltops, piers — that show a meditate prompt when you get close. Visit each one and use the prompt; it usually takes a few seconds, so do not walk away mid-meditation or it may not count. There is no combat involved — it is a calm exploration task, best done while working through The Goodtime State, since both trophies reward visiting the same far corners of the map. The total number of spots was not confirmed at launch, so check the in-game meditation list or menu to see how many are left, and remember the remote spots are the ones players miss: check the map's far corners, not just Vice City.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Fair Game is the trophy for hunting a unique animal for Bret. Bret's hunting thread asks for a specific rare animal — track it using the hunting clues (tracks, calls, habitat) rather than wandering the woods at random. Bring a scoped rifle, approach downwind, and take a clean shot; a unique animal will not respawn quickly if you spook it, so save first in a fresh slot before the final approach. Crouch and move slowly, use cover and the wind indicator if the game shows one, and take the shot only when you are sure of the target — wounding a unique animal and losing it is the worst outcome, worse than missing entirely. Once the animal is down, return the kill to Bret to complete the hunt and pop the trophy.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Don't Touch My Deck is the silver for completing 3 Collectible Card sets. Cards are hidden across Leonida — in shops, bars, landmarks and out-of-the-way spots — and a set is complete when you own every card in it; three finished sets trigger the trophy. Collect as you explore and use the in-game collection screen to see which sets are nearly done, then hunt the missing cards in those sets first: finishing a set you are one card short of is worth more than starting a new one. Duplicates do not help, so ignore them and focus on the gaps, and remember cards hide in interiors too — shops and bars, not just landmarks. The collection screen is your map for this trophy: chase the sets with one or two cards missing.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: You WAiNKer! is the silver for WAiNK-ing it at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game social app, and 'WAiNK It' means checking in or posting from a location. Visit 100 distinct spots — landmarks, businesses, viewpoints — and WAiNK from each; the same location twice does not count, so keep moving. It stacks with exploration for The Goodtime State, so do both together and tick locations off as you travel. A good rhythm is to WAiNK at every stop on a road trip — fuel stops, landmarks, viewpoints — rather than grinding 100 check-ins in one sitting, which turns a pleasant exploration trophy into a chore. Check your WAiNK count in the app to see how many are left.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: One Last Thing wants 50 completed challenges. Challenges are the game's mini-objectives — driving, combat, exploration and activity feats listed in the Challenges menu — and they accumulate naturally across a full playthrough, so do not grind them early. If you are short at the end, open the menu, pick the easiest unfinished ones (short drives, easy shots) and grind them out; sort the menu by progress if it allows it, because the challenges closest to done are the cheapest wins. Story, strangers and activities complete most of them for free, so check the Challenges menu after each roadmap stage — you will usually be closer than you think, and the last ten are the only ones that feel like a grind at all.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Hot Together is the trophy for losing a 4-star wanted level with your partner and escaping the heat — and it is flagged here as POSSIBLY MISSABLE, because it needs a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, which mostly happens during partner missions, and the community has not yet confirmed whether a 4-star escape can be arranged in free roam after the story. The safe play: make a manual save before every partner mission, and the first time you hit 4 stars together, go for it immediately — break line of sight, get out of the search area, and hide until the stars clear. A parking garage, an alley or a tunnel all work, and a fast car helps you leave the search cone quickly. If the moment passes and the mission ends, reload the save and retry rather than hoping for another chance later. Unverified at the time of writing, so treat the warning as cheap insurance.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Retail Therapy wants three shop robberies back-to-back with your partner, without losing your wanted level — and it is flagged here as POSSIBLY MISSABLE for the same reason as Hot Together: it needs your partner present, which mostly happens during partner missions, and the community has not yet confirmed a free-roam way to arrange it after the story. The trick is the 'back-to-back' part: rob a shop, keep the wanted level alive, drive straight to the next shop and rob it, then the third — if the wanted level clears between robberies, the chain breaks and you start over. Pick three shops close together on the map before you start, use a fast car, and do not stop to fight the police between shops. Save before the attempt so a broken chain costs you a reload, not a playthrough.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Whip It Good wants 100 vehicles discovered. Discovery counts when you get close to a new vehicle type — driving past a parked car you have never seen before usually counts — so the trick is variety, not mileage: drive through different districts, visit car parks, dealerships and the docks, and hop into anything unusual you see. The count is tracked in the game, so check it in Stats or the vehicle menu to see how far along you are. It stacks beautifully with the exploration and WAiNK trophies: one long road trip through every district, stopping at car parks and landmarks, can push all three counts at once. Rare and special vehicles count the same as common ones, so do not chase exotics — chase variety.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Gunslinger wants five enemies taken down in a single use of Combat Focus — the slow-motion aiming mode. The setup matters more than the aim: find a firefight with at least five enemies grouped together, trigger Combat Focus when they are all visible, and work through them methodically instead of spraying. A rifle or a good automatic weapon helps, and headshots drop enemies faster, which matters because Combat Focus does not last forever. Good spots are the bigger story shootouts and gang-operation raids, where enemies arrive in groups — Operation Savage Glory is a natural place to try it. If you only get three or four, reload a checkpoint and try again in the same fight rather than hunting for a new one; the trophy is about one clean run, not five scattered kills.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Catch Me If You Can wants an unscheduled departure at VCIA — steal a plane at Vice City International Airport and take off without filing a flight plan, in other words. Get into the airport (the VCIA Takedown story mission teaches you the layout — note where the planes park while you are there), find a plane on the runway or apron, get in, and take off while the airport police are still reacting. A small fast plane is easier to steal and lift than a big one, and taking off into open sky beats trying to thread the runways. Expect a wanted level the moment you climb into the cockpit; the trophy should pop once you are airborne and clear of the airport, so do not bail out early — stay with the plane until the notification appears, then land somewhere quiet or just enjoy the flight.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Challenging Tank is the Rhino tank trophy — the description's wink tells you the job: get into a Rhino tank and make it count. Rhinos turn up at military areas and in high-wanted-level responses, so the practical route is to build heat until the army answers, then take the tank when it arrives — or find one parked at a military site and drive it out. Once you are in the driver's seat, the tank does the work: its cannon clears roadblocks and its armour shrugs off small arms, so drive through the city and let the wanted level climb. The exact trigger was not fully confirmed at launch — whether it needs a kill count, a survival time, or simply driving the tank — so watch for the trophy notification as you go, and keep the rampage going until it pops rather than bailing out after thirty seconds.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Sneakthief wants a jewelry store robbed without being detected — the quiet version of a robbery, and the opposite of the loud approach most GTA players default to. Go in quiet: move slowly, stay out of the staff's line of sight, take the goods without smashing a case in front of a witness, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. A suppressed weapon and a mask help if the game offers them, and a fast car parked close by matters for the exit even on a clean job — detection can still happen on the way out. If you are spotted, do not fight it out and hope: leave, lose the heat, and try again another day, because a detected robbery does not count and a shootout in a jewelry store rarely ends quietly. Save before the attempt so a blown run costs you a reload.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Maximum Withdrawal is the silver for robbing 5 bank vaults and escaping. Bank vaults are the big robbery targets — plan each one like a small heist: scout the bank, pick your entry, grab the vault's contents and escape clean, because the robbery only counts if you get away. Five successful vault jobs trigger the trophy, and the vaults are spread across Leonida, so each one is a different drive and a different escape route. Bring armour and a good weapon for the getaway, keep a fast car nearby, and do not linger inside after the vault is open — the longer you stay, the heavier the response. Space the jobs out between other cleanup work rather than doing all five back-to-back; the heat and the planning both get easier with a breather between jobs.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: A Classic Blitz Play is the trophy for robbing an armored truck and escaping — the classic GTA side job, and a nod to the series' most famous heist. Armored trucks run set routes around Leonida: find one on the road, stop it, crack it open and take the cash, then escape before the response closes in. The stop is the hard part — a moving truck does not want to stop — so use a heavy vehicle to block it or a sticky approach that forces it off the road, then work fast once it is still. Keep a fast getaway car ready and break line of sight quickly after the grab; the trophy pops once you have escaped, not when you crack the truck, so the getaway is the job. If the first truck gets away, another will come along the same routes.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: The Goodtime State wants all of Leonida explored — every region of the map revealed. The trick is systematic coverage, not wandering: drive the highways to the far corners, then sweep the back roads and the coastline, because the map fills in as you travel and the last few percent always hides in a corner you never had a reason to visit. It stacks with the meditation spots, the WAiNK locations and the vehicle discoveries, so one long road trip can push four trophies at once: stop at every viewpoint, WAiNK at every landmark, meditate at every spot and drive past every car park. Check the map regularly for grey areas — those are the places you still need to go — and remember the islands and the far north, which are easy to skip when the story keeps you in Vice City.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Pest Control wants an illegal operation robbed for each gang in Leonida — one raid per gang, not one raid total. Illegal operations are the gangs' off-the-books businesses: stash houses, chop shops, smuggling depots. Scout each one first, because every gang defends its turf differently — some with numbers, some with heavy weapons, some with a maze of a building — and plan your entry and exit before you go in loud. Bring armour and a good rifle, hit fast, grab the take and get out; the trophy pops once every gang has been hit once. The exact list of gangs was not fully confirmed at launch, so check the in-game information or the operation markers to see which gangs are left, and do not assume a gang is done until the game says so.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: In The Beginning… is the quiet trophy: enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to Ocean Beach — the Vice City beachfront — find a bar or a spot with a view of the water, and order a cocktail. The trophy is about the moment, not a challenge: sit, drink, watch the ocean, and let it pop. The ellipsis in the name hints at a story beat, so if the prompt does not appear on your first visit, try it at a different time of day or after more story progress — the game may only offer the moment once the story has reached a certain point. Either way it costs you ten quiet minutes and a drink, and it is the most relaxing trophy in the whole list.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Capital Offense wants you to smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — the GTA signature move: drive a car straight through the showroom glass. Find a vehicle showroom, get a car inside (or steal the show car), and drive it out through the front window. The trick is the approach: you need enough run-up inside the showroom to build speed, or enough speed outside to punch through, and the classic style is a straight line through the glass, not a slow push through the door. Expect a wanted level and a shower of glass — that is the point — and a repair bill afterwards, so do it in a car you do not mind scratching. If the first showroom's layout fights you, try another one: the trophy is about the exit, not the building.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Let’s Go Bowling is the trophy for a follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — a GTA nod to the series' most famous bowling date. Head to the Kolt & Associates alley, rent a lane and bowl a game; the trophy is about the follow-through, so play the game properly rather than throwing gutter balls for a laugh. Bowling uses a simple aim-and-power mechanic: line the shot up, pick a steady power, and release cleanly — a few practice throws teach you the timing faster than any guide can. You do not need a perfect game or a high score, just a completed game with a proper follow-through, and the trophy pops at the end of the game. It pairs naturally with Ten Pin, the trophy for bowling people over with a melee drive-by, so do both while you are in a bowling mood.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Personal Best is the cryptic one: 'a partnership with mass appeal.' The description points at doing something with your partner that the public notices — most likely a social-media or fame thread, where you and your partner build an audience together. The honest status at launch is that the exact trigger was not yet pinned down by the community, so treat this guide entry as a lead, not a recipe: look for a partnership or follower mechanic in the phone's social apps, build it with your partner, and watch for the trophy as the audience grows. Check the in-game trackers and the social apps for a count or a milestone — a follower total, a viral post, a joint appearance — and chase the milestone the game shows you rather than guessing. If the trigger turns out to be something else entirely, the in-game hints are the authority.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Actions Speak Louder is the trophy for choices made, for better or worse — and it is flagged here as POSSIBLY MISSABLE, because it reads like a story-choice trophy: at some point in the story you will be offered a choice, and this trophy pops for making it (or for making a particular one). The exact choice was not confirmed at launch, so the safe play is the same as for the finale: keep a manual save before every mission that offers a visible choice, make the choice, and check whether the trophy pops. If it does not, reload the save and take the other path. Do not play the whole story without saving before choices — a second playthrough for one choice is the most expensive mistake in this list. If both paths turn out to pop it, you have lost nothing but a save slot.

Make the choice when it is offered
Check whether the trophy pops
If it does not, reload the save and take the other path
tips: Save before choices, not after them — the save is the only way back
The finale is the most likely place for the choice, so guard the pre-finale save

Playing the whole story on autosave alone and discovering the choice too late

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.time: At a story choice or retry
trophies.guide: Bad Luck, I Guess — 'second time's the charm' — reads like the sibling of Actions Speak Louder: a trophy for a second attempt at something, most likely retrying a story choice or a failed approach and getting it right the second time. It is flagged here as POSSIBLY MISSABLE for the same reason: if it hinges on a one-time choice, there may be no second chance without a save. The practical approach is the same: keep a manual save before every choice mission, and if a choice goes wrong — or a mission fails in a way that feels like it mattered — reload and try the other path rather than pushing on. The exact trigger was not confirmed at launch, so treat this as a guarded guess: save often, retry deliberately, and let the trophy surprise you when the second attempt lands.

If a choice or attempt goes wrong, reload the save
Take the other path or retry the approach
The trophy pops when the second attempt lands

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The Truth Is Out There — 'what the hell just happened?' — is the game's weird-encounter trophy, the classic GTA easter-egg hunt: a UFO, a strange light, a mysterious figure, something that makes you say exactly what the description says. These encounters usually hide in remote places at odd hours — a hilltop at night, a desert road after midnight, a swamp under a full moon — and the community was still mapping them at launch, so the honest advice is to explore the strange corners of Leonida at night and watch the sky. Check community maps once they exist, but do not trust a location until someone has confirmed it in-game; and when you find something odd, stop and watch it — the trophy pops for witnessing the encounter, not for shooting at it.

Watch the sky and the horizon for strange lights or figures
Stop and witness the encounter when you find one
The trophy pops for seeing it — do not shoot first

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Ten Pin wants you to bowl people over with a melee drive-by — knocking pedestrians down like bowling pins from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon. The setup is a slow drive through a crowded area with a melee weapon ready: swing as you pass, and the game counts the people you bowl over. A slow car or a bike works best — too fast and you will miss the swing, too slow and the crowd scatters. Bowling alleys and busy sidewalks are the natural hunting grounds, and the name is a pun on the bowling trophy (Let’s Go Bowling), so do both while you are in a bowling mood. You do not need ten in one pass — the trophy counts the drive-by as a whole — but a crowded street and a steady swing make it pop fast. Mind the wanted level: bowling people over attracts police, so plan your exit.
steps: Take a slow car or a bike with a melee weapon ready
Drive slowly through a crowded area
Swing the melee weapon as you pass people
The trophy pops when the drive-by bowls enough of them over

Busy sidewalks and bowling-alley crowds are the best hunting grounds
pitfalls: Driving too fast through the crowd — you will miss every swing
Forgetting the wanted level: bowling people over attracts police, so plan your exit

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Dime on the Dollar wants $250,000 earned by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty money from heists and robberies — the Cartel Heist, the bank vaults, the gang operations — and they need washing before they spend clean. Find your laundering contacts (the game introduces them through the story and the stranger threads) and run the bills through them regularly, a little at a time, rather than hoarding a mountain of marked cash and trying to wash it all at once: contacts have limits, and a steady flow earns faster than a single huge wash. The total is cumulative across the whole game, so every heist and robbery feeds it — keep robbing, keep laundering, and check the count in the game to see how close you are. The heist payouts alone get you a long way there.

Find your laundering contacts through the story and stranger threads
Launder the bills regularly, a little at a time
Check the count in the game; the trophy pops at $250,000 laundered

pitfalls: Hoarding marked cash instead of laundering it — unwashed bills do not count
Spending dirty money directly: it needs washing through contacts first

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Treat Yo Self wants $100,000 spent across all shops — clothes, weapons, ammo, cars, food, whatever the shops of Leonida sell. The total is cumulative and counts everything you buy anywhere, so most players will be most of the way there by the end of the story without trying: ammo, armour, clothes and car upgrades all count. If you are short at the end, the fastest top-up is the expensive stuff — a high-end car, a full weapon loadout, a wardrobe refresh — bought in one shopping trip. Do not waste money early just for this trophy; spend normally through the story and the grind, and only top up deliberately at the end if the count is short. Check the total in the game before you go on a spree, so you buy exactly what you still need.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Little Boxes wants all garage properties purchased — every garage the game sells, bought and owned. Garages are the property thread: they give you somewhere to store the cars you collect, and the trophy counts owning the full set. The exact number of garages was not confirmed at launch, so check the in-game property or real-estate menu for the list and buy them one by one — the game will show you which ones you still need. They are not cheap as a set, so do this after the story when the heist money is in: the Cartel Heist payout and the laundered bills from Dime on the Dollar are the natural funding. Buy the cheapest first if cash is tight, and remember a garage is also practical — it is where the cars for Whip It Good and the races live.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: On the Spot wants 10 vehicles registered to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game vehicle-sharing app. Registering a vehicle means adding it to the app so it can be called or shared: drive or take a vehicle, open the Scooter Bros app on the phone, and register it. Ten different vehicles trigger the trophy, so variety is the job — register the cars, bikes and oddities you find around Leonida rather than the same car ten times. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good, the trophy for discovering 100 vehicles: every new vehicle you discover is a candidate for registration, so register as you discover and both counts climb together. The app itself unlocks through the story or the phone's app list — if it is not there yet, push the story forward.

Register a vehicle you own or have found
Repeat with 10 different vehicles — variety counts
The trophy pops at the tenth registration
